project.name: Bunya-Jido
project.summary: A grounded semantic repository map that publishes evidence-linked architecture and bounded coding-agent routes, with an optional guarded Codex execution boundary.
project.architecture_style: Offline semantic projection with deterministic support, explicit trust gates, and guarded local execution.
project.thesis: Bunya-Jido publishes evidence-linked repository interpretations as offline maps and bounded coding-agent context, and can execute that context through a guarded Codex runner only after explicit trust and worktree gates pass.

planes.label: Execution
planes.purpose: Guarded local process execution and evidence capture.

planes.label: Trust And Quality
planes.purpose: Grounding, readability, benchmark, and regression checks.

nodes.label: Command Line Interface
nodes.description: Dispatches build, validation, preparation, trusted context, guarded Codex execution, benchmark audit, and safe-and-resolved token/time reporting commands.
nodes.why_it_matters: Every published artifact or agent-context request begins at an explicit command boundary.
nodes.inspector_summary: Command entrypoints coordinate publication and diagnostics without defining the trust policy.

nodes.label: Guarded Codex Run
nodes.description: Maps compact context decisions to a non-escalating Codex sandbox, requires a clean baseline for launch, captures JSONL process evidence, and audits semantic production boundaries.
nodes.why_it_matters: It turns route advice into a reviewable local run without letting non-MATCH decisions become writable.
nodes.inspector_summary: Only MATCH receives workspace-write; fake-executable tests prove orchestration and audit behavior, not a live Codex OS sandbox.
inputs: Optional model, executable, output directory, and timeout
outputs: Markdown report and captured process streams
constraints: Actual execution requires a clean Git baseline.
Non-MATCH decisions remain read-only without an escalation option.
Safe-edit paths guide and audit activity but do not grant OS access.
Live nested Codex execution requires separate human approval during Build Week.

nodes.label: Static Scanner
nodes.description: Creates deterministic scan graphs and provenance-tagged supporting repository observations.
nodes.inspector_summary: Static observations assist authoring; generated example provider hints are excluded from Studio landmarks.

nodes.label: Blueprint Projection
nodes.description: Loads semantic artifacts and produces the published graph contract, including Studio projections, decision records, and scenario metadata.
nodes.why_it_matters: It turns reviewed semantic inputs into the graph payload later consumers are allowed to inspect.
nodes.inspector_summary: Blueprint publication preserves validated Studio editorial choices, atlas data, and task-route projections.

nodes.label: Grounding Gate
nodes.description: Blocks semantic publication when core evidence, critical relationships, Studio decision records, or v2 atlas contracts cannot be trusted.
nodes.why_it_matters: It is the boundary that prevents an attractive map from being published as trusted without evidence.
nodes.inspector_summary: Validation resolves evidence and Studio contract references, including declared primary-selection consistency, before normal publication may continue.

nodes.label: Atlas Quality Evaluator
nodes.description: Measures deterministic Studio readability and scenario-policy signals while surfacing missing decision rationale and misleading narration as review-required interpretation.
nodes.inspector_summary: Quality diagnostics measure visible density, narration honesty, and recorded editorial context; optional reports expose review work without proving preference.

nodes.label: Benchmark Evidence Suite
nodes.description: Exercises Studio generality and provides auditable worktree plus safe-and-resolved token/time evidence for live benchmark runners.
nodes.inspector_summary: Benchmark evidence keeps workspace truth, unsafe or unresolved exclusions, explicit repeated-run pairing, map-authoring cost, and task-efficiency comparisons visible.

nodes.label: Agent Route Parity
nodes.description: Validates bounded task routes against semantic nodes, workflows, required reading, tests, and optional Studio reading context.
nodes.inspector_summary: Only grounded route and projection/scenario references can reach agent context or appear as trusted viewer paths.

nodes.label: Trusted Context Generator
nodes.description: Classifies task scope conservatively, emits compact selected-route guidance by default, and provides bounded read-only discovery when an in-scope repair has no trusted route.
nodes.inspector_summary: Context generation keeps P1/P2 safety and recovery guidance in compact output, while verbose output retains diagnostics and full discovery evidence.

nodes.label: HTML Renderer
nodes.description: Embeds the published graph payload into a standalone offline HTML artifact.
nodes.why_it_matters: It carries only validated graph data into the portable human-facing output.
nodes.inspector_summary: The renderer safely embeds data; it does not reinterpret or improve semantic trust.

nodes.label: Interactive Viewer
nodes.description: Displays human-first repository orientation, semantic inspector context, trust, evidence, Studio projections, contextual navigation, validated narrated scenario playback, and copyable trusted agent-route context offline.
nodes.why_it_matters: It is how people first understand and then inspect the map while preserving the provenance and limitations of authored claims.
inputs: Validated projections, workflows, scenarios, and task routes
constraints: Presentation must not become evidence or reinterpret authored claims.
Human orientation must preserve the existing canvas-first visual design.
nodes.inspector_summary: The viewer gives people a repository summary, outline, directional path cues, semantic inspector cards, and evidence-backed playback without becoming evidence.

nodes.label: Semantic Contract Tests
nodes.description: Exercises grounding publication gates, guarded Codex execution, Studio contracts, benchmark evidence reporting, viewer playback surfaces, and agent-map parity behavior.
nodes.inspector_summary: Regression tests make the public self-map and viewer contract repeatable in CI.

nodes.label: Continuous Integration
nodes.description: Runs the test and release-gate contract on supported Python versions.
nodes.inspector_summary: CI repeats mechanical gates; maintainers still review editorial quality.

nodes.label: Public Product Contract
nodes.description: Explains artifact modes, Studio scenario expectations, guarded Codex execution, quality review reporting, trust boundaries, and command usage.
nodes.inspector_summary: Public onboarding documents declared behavior and limitations.

nodes.label: Contribution Roadmap
nodes.description: Defines staged work and acceptance criteria for grounded semantic maps.
nodes.inspector_summary: Roadmap detail remains inspectable but is not a first-screen product landmark.

workflows.label: Static Evidence Discovery
workflows.description: Collect bounded discovery evidence while preserving provider-hint origin and excluding generated example pollution.
workflows.trigger: bunya-jido scan or semantic build with contextual overlay
workflows.outcome: Static observations whose provider hints carry inspectable provenance.

workflows.label: Semantic Map Publication
workflows.description: Build a grounded semantic graph and expose its trust state and qualified narration in offline HTML.

workflows.label: Task Route Publication
workflows.description: Validate agent routes and their optional Studio reading context before showing them as viewer paths or copyable agent guidance.
workflows.outcome: Trusted task-route presets with bounded optional Studio context.

workflows.label: Trusted Context Generation
workflows.description: Validate blueprint and route trust, classify request scope and route sufficiency, then emit compact trusted-route guidance or capped evidence-backed read-only discovery.
workflows.outcome: A compact decision-aware handoff where only MATCH exposes route and safe-edit guidance, while verbose diagnostics remain opt-in.

workflows.label: Guarded Codex Run
workflows.description: Select non-escalating sandbox policy from compact context, require a clean baseline, capture a local Codex process, and audit observed plus final production activity.
workflows.outcome: A schema v1 run report whose success requires context policy, process completion, complete JSONL, and production boundary compliance.

workflows.label: Continuous Contract Check
workflows.description: Run characterization and golden checks in CI against the published semantic contract.

workflows.label: Atlas Quality Evaluation
workflows.description: Measure Studio overview and scenario narration signals while exposing interpretation that still needs human review.
workflows.outcome: Objective metrics, separated review warnings, and optional local Markdown review output.

workflows.label: Benchmark Evidence Reporting
workflows.description: Audit live-run workspace truth and compare only explicitly paired safe-and-resolved token/time results.
workflows.outcome: Auditable production activity, exclusions, medians, p90s, savings, and break-even counts without benchmark-specific routing tuning.

workflows.label: Studio Benchmark Review
workflows.description: Exercise differing atlas theses and scenario policies without introducing a domain seed.

decision_record.repository_thesis_summary: Bunya-Jido publishes evidence-linked repository interpretations as offline maps and bounded coding-agent context, and can execute that context through a guarded Codex runner only after explicit trust and worktree gates pass.

projection_candidates.label: Trusted Publication
projection_candidates.question_answered: How is a semantic map permitted to reach readers?
distortion_risks: Bounded agent navigation may appear secondary unless retained as an authored alternate view.
projection_candidates.selection_reason: It explains the shared human and coding-agent artifact while keeping evidence and publication gates visible first.

projection_candidates.label: Bounded Agent Navigation
projection_candidates.question_answered: How can a coding agent receive a trusted route, bounded read-only discovery, honest rejection, or guarded local execution?
distortion_risks: It could make the human-facing map look like a secondary product surface.
Fake-executable evidence could be mistaken for live Codex sandbox proof.
projection_candidates.selection_reason: It remains an important alternate view, but does not introduce the shared artifact as clearly as Trusted Publication.

projection_candidates.label: Quality Contract
projection_candidates.question_answered: Which checks keep the Studio output honest?
distortion_risks: It over-centralizes validation machinery over the published map experience.
projection_candidates.selection_reason: It supports publication trust and belongs as a secondary quality-focused projection.

scenario_candidates.label: Publish A Trusted Map
scenario_candidates.reason: It follows the documented build, validation, and render path with source-backed steps.

scenario_candidates.label: Request Bounded Agent Context
scenario_candidates.reason: It follows the documented route-validation path from a task request to bounded guidance.

over_centralization_risks.risk: Static evidence collection could be mistaken for the authored product meaning.
over_centralization_risks.mitigation: Keep scanner evidence contextual and outside the primary landmark path.

over_centralization_risks.risk: Automation could appear to prove editorial truth rather than repeat deterministic checks.
over_centralization_risks.mitigation: Keep CI contextual and state that projection quality remains review-required.

over_centralization_risks.risk: A guarded runner could be mistaken for proof that a live nested Codex sandbox was exercised.
over_centralization_risks.mitigation: Keep fake-executable orchestration evidence distinct from separately approved live-run evidence.
